assumptions: The failing code is assumed to be the account-page spend calculation introduced behind the flag; this is inferred from the error type and timing, not from reading the code or a stack trace.

No deployment for io-shop appears in the change record over the six weeks reviewed (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-12), so the flag toggle is assumed to be the only change in play. If the defect was shipped by an unrecorded deploy, the flag only made it reachable.

The `UpstreamTimeout: payment authorization timed out` errors are assumed to be unrelated background noise: they appear at the same rate before, during, and after onset and do not explain the step change.

The incident is recorded as ended at 15:23:21Z, but no evidence in the logs supports recovery: the flag still reads `on` and ZeroDivisionErrors are still present in the final minute of logs read (15:22). The end timestamp is assumed to reflect alert closure, not confirmed customer-facing recovery.
The attempted mitigation is assumed not to have contributed to any recovery, since the flag was returned to `on` at 15:21:49Z.

Log sampling is assumed representative; the per-minute lines show a constant 200 flag evaluations per minute and only a couple of example error lines per minute, so they were not used to reconstruct impact.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, a newly enabled option in the online shop's account area caused a large share of customers' account pages to fail to load. The problem began at about 15:09 UTC, when the option was switched on for a portion of visitors, and affected all visitors from 15:10; automated monitoring raised an alert at 15:14 and the incident was recorded as ending at 15:23, roughly a quarter of an hour later. Customers trying to view their account page during that window saw errors; other parts of the shop were not implicated. The automated responder correctly identified the newly enabled option as the cause within a minute, but its attempt to switch the option back off did not stick — the option was left switched on, and the failures were still present in the last logs available. The incident was escalated to humans with the cause identified and the fix still outstanding.
input.root_cause: Enabling the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop exposed a divide-by-zero defect in the account-page spend calculation: the flag began evaluating `on` for part of traffic at 15:09 and for all traffic from 15:10, and from that moment account page requests began failing with `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`, an error type absent from the logs whenever the flag is off. The one remediation attempt did not hold — the change log shows Argus's final action at 15:21:49Z set the flag back ON, and every log line after that still reads `monthly-spend-feature=on`, so the faulty code path was never actually disabled during the incident.
